meta.name: Queue OpenAI-compatible LLM chat requests with PostgreSQL and a local GPU

name: Queue OpenAI-compatible LLM requests in PostgreSQL

parameters.content:
## Queue OpenAI-compatible LLM requests in PostgreSQL

### How it works

This workflow implements an OpenAI-compatible chat completions gateway backed by a PostgreSQL queue. Incoming requests can be validated, enqueued, queried, canceled, or listed, while a scheduled dispatcher claims queued jobs and sends them to an upstream LLM endpoint. Additional webhooks expose task status and configured model metadata.

### Setup steps

- Configure PostgreSQL credentials for all Postgres nodes and run the manual setup path once to create the queue table and indexes.
- Set the public webhook URLs for the chat completions, task status, and models endpoints according to your n8n deployment.
- Configure the upstream OpenAI-compatible chat completions URL, timeout, lease duration, and retry settings in the GPU dispatcher configuration node.
- Add any required upstream authentication headers or credentials to the HTTP request node that calls the LLM provider.
- Set the supported model IDs in the model discovery configuration node.

### Customization

Adjust polling limits, job retry attempts, lease duration, retry backoff, and configured model IDs to match your expected workload and upstream LLM capacity.

## Initialize queue schema

Manual setup cluster that creates the PostgreSQL queue table and indexes, then reports setup completion.

## Receive chat request

Accepts OpenAI-style chat completion requests, applies gateway settings, normalizes the payload, and routes the request type.

## Return chat response

Converges all chat gateway branches, formats the output as JSON or SSE-compatible content, and returns the webhook response.

## Validate status request

Receives task status lookup requests, validates the task ID, and decides whether to read from the database or immediately return an error.

## Return task status

Fetches task status details from PostgreSQL, formats them, and sends the status webhook response.

## Expose model list

Handles the models endpoint by loading configured model IDs, formatting them, and returning an OpenAI-compatible model list.

## Claim queued jobs

Scheduled dispatcher cluster that runs every few seconds, applies dispatcher settings, recovers expired leases, and claims the oldest available task.

parameters.query:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS llm_queue_jobs (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY CHECK (id ~ '^task_[a-f0-9]{32}$'),
  request_body JSONB NOT NULL,
  model TEXT NOT NULL,
  status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'queued'
    CHECK (status IN ('queued', 'running', 'succeeded', 'failed', 'cancelled', 'expired')),
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  available_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  started_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  completed_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  lease_expires_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  attempts INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (attempts >= 0),
  max_attempts INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 3 CHECK (max_attempts > 0),
  claim_token TEXT,
  response_body JSONB,
  error_body JSONB,
  waiting_tool_name TEXT,
  waiting_tool_arg TEXT,
  waiting_tool_call_id TEXT,
  wait_poll_seconds INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 5 CHECK (wait_poll_seconds BETWEEN 1 AND 60),
  wait_max_attempts INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 720 CHECK (wait_max_attempts BETWEEN 1 AND 8640),
  CONSTRAINT llm_queue_terminal_result CHECK (
    status <> 'succeeded' OR response_body IS NOT NULL
  )
);

ALTER TABLE llm_queue_jobs
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS wait_poll_seconds INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 5,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS wait_max_attempts INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 720;

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS llm_queue_jobs_ready_idx
  ON llm_queue_jobs (available_at, created_at, id)
  WHERE status = 'queued';

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS llm_queue_jobs_running_idx
  ON llm_queue_jobs (lease_expires_at)
  WHERE status = 'running';

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS llm_queue_jobs_created_idx
  ON llm_queue_jobs (created_at DESC);

COMMENT ON TABLE llm_queue_jobs IS
  'Durable FIFO queue for the Wetomate queued OpenAI-compatible gateway';

SELECT 'llm_queue_jobs is ready' AS message;

SELECT
  $1::TEXT AS requested_id,
  $2::TEXT AS lookup_source,
  job.id AS task_id,
  job.model,
  job.status,
  job.created_at,
  job.started_at,
  job.completed_at,
  job.attempts,
  job.max_attempts,
  job.response_body,
  job.error_body,
  job.waiting_tool_name,
  job.waiting_tool_arg,
  job.wait_poll_seconds,
  job.wait_max_attempts,
  CASE
    WHEN job.status = 'queued' THEN 1 + (
      SELECT COUNT(*)
      FROM llm_queue_jobs ahead
      WHERE ahead.status = 'queued'
        AND ahead.available_at <= NOW()
        AND (ahead.created_at, ahead.id) < (job.created_at, job.id)
    )
    ELSE NULL
  END AS position
FROM (SELECT 1) singleton
LEFT JOIN llm_queue_jobs job ON job.id = $1
LIMIT 1;

WITH updated AS (
  UPDATE llm_queue_jobs
  SET status = 'cancelled', completed_at = NOW()
  WHERE id = $1 AND status = 'queued'
  RETURNING id, model, status
), selected AS (
  SELECT * FROM updated
  UNION ALL
  SELECT id, model, status
  FROM llm_queue_jobs
  WHERE id = $1 AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM updated)
  LIMIT 1
)
SELECT $1::TEXT AS requested_id, selected.id AS task_id, selected.model, selected.status
FROM (SELECT 1) singleton
LEFT JOIN selected ON TRUE;

SELECT COALESCE(
  JSONB_AGG(
    JSONB_BUILD_OBJECT(
      'task_id', id,
      'model', model,
      'status', status,
      'created_at', created_at,
      'started_at', started_at
    ) ORDER BY created_at DESC
  ),
  '[]'::JSONB
) AS jobs
FROM (
  SELECT id, model, status, created_at, started_at
  FROM llm_queue_jobs
  WHERE status IN ('queued', 'running')
  ORDER BY created_at DESC
  LIMIT 50
) active_jobs;

INSERT INTO llm_queue_jobs (
  id,
  request_body,
  model,
  waiting_tool_name,
  waiting_tool_arg,
  max_attempts,
  wait_poll_seconds,
  wait_max_attempts
)
VALUES (
  'task_' || REPLACE(GEN_RANDOM_UUID()::TEXT, '-', ''),
  $1::JSONB,
  $2,
  NULLIF($3, ''),
  NULLIF($4, ''),
  $5::INTEGER,
  $6::INTEGER,
  $7::INTEGER
)
RETURNING id AS task_id, model, status, created_at, waiting_tool_name, waiting_tool_arg,
  max_attempts, wait_poll_seconds, wait_max_attempts;

SELECT
  $1::TEXT AS requested_id,
  job.id AS task_id,
  job.model,
  job.status,
  job.created_at,
  job.started_at,
  job.completed_at,
  job.attempts,
  job.max_attempts,
  job.response_body ->> 'id' AS response_id,
  job.error_body,
  CASE
    WHEN job.status = 'queued' THEN 1 + (
      SELECT COUNT(*)
      FROM llm_queue_jobs ahead
      WHERE ahead.status = 'queued'
        AND ahead.available_at <= NOW()
        AND (ahead.created_at, ahead.id) < (job.created_at, job.id)
    )
    ELSE NULL
  END AS position
FROM (SELECT 1) singleton
LEFT JOIN llm_queue_jobs job ON job.id = $1
LIMIT 1;

WITH recovered AS (
  UPDATE llm_queue_jobs
  SET
    status = CASE WHEN attempts < max_attempts THEN 'queued' ELSE 'failed' END,
    available_at = CASE WHEN attempts < max_attempts THEN NOW() + INTERVAL '30 seconds' ELSE available_at END,
    completed_at = CASE WHEN attempts < max_attempts THEN NULL ELSE NOW() END,
    claim_token = NULL,
    lease_expires_at = NULL,
    error_body = JSONB_BUILD_OBJECT(
      'type', 'lease_expired',
      'message', 'The dispatcher execution ended before recording a result.'
    )
  WHERE status = 'running' AND lease_expires_at < NOW()
  RETURNING id
)
SELECT COUNT(*)::INTEGER AS recovered_jobs FROM recovered;

WITH lock_attempt AS (
  SELECT PG_TRY_ADVISORY_XACT_LOCK(71001) AS acquired
), candidate AS (
  SELECT job.id
  FROM llm_queue_jobs job
  WHERE job.status = 'queued'
    AND job.available_at <= NOW()
    AND (SELECT acquired FROM lock_attempt)
    AND NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM llm_queue_jobs active
      WHERE active.status = 'running' AND active.lease_expires_at > NOW()
    )
  ORDER BY job.created_at, job.id
  FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
  LIMIT 1
), claimed AS (
  UPDATE llm_queue_jobs job
  SET
    status = 'running',
    started_at = NOW(),
    completed_at = NULL,
    attempts = job.attempts + 1,
    claim_token = REPLACE(GEN_RANDOM_UUID()::TEXT, '-', ''),
    lease_expires_at = NOW() + MAKE_INTERVAL(mins => $1::INTEGER),
    error_body = NULL
  WHERE job.id = (SELECT id FROM candidate)
  RETURNING job.*
)
SELECT
  claimed.*,
  (claimed.request_body - 'stream_options') || JSONB_BUILD_OBJECT('stream', FALSE) AS dispatch_body
FROM claimed;

UPDATE llm_queue_jobs
SET
  status = $3,
  response_body = CASE WHEN $3 = 'succeeded' THEN $4::JSONB ELSE NULL END,
  error_body = CASE WHEN $3 <> 'succeeded' THEN $5::JSONB ELSE NULL END,
  available_at = CASE WHEN $3 = 'queued' THEN NOW() + MAKE_INTERVAL(secs => $6::INTEGER) ELSE available_at END,
  completed_at = CASE WHEN $3 IN ('succeeded', 'failed') THEN NOW() ELSE NULL END,
  claim_token = NULL,
  lease_expires_at = NULL
WHERE id = $1 AND claim_token = $2
RETURNING id AS task_id, status, attempts, completed_at;
